// diagnostic

E-APP-TARGET-FEATURE

App feature `.{feature}` needs target `{required}`, but the resolved target is `{target}`.

What

App feature `.{feature}` needs target `{required}`, but the resolved target is `{target}`.

Why

App is one type across targets, but each feature must be supported by the target selected by `#Target` or the package manifest; rejecting it in sema keeps AOT, JIT, interpreter, and web codegen on one meaning (I9).

Fix

Choose a build target that supports `.{feature}` (for example `#Target(JS)` for browser features or a native target for server features), or remove that feature.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E-APP-TARGET-FEATURE: tests/ui/app_capability_target.stderr.

Error [E-WEB-TARGET-BROWSER]: `run` is pinned to Wasm but uses the `Browser` effect
  --> tests/ui/app_capability_target.jet:4:4
    |
  4 | fn run() App -> web.app().csr()
    |    ^^^
 Why: the web backend keeps DOM/view code in JS and compute in WASM; a Wasm-pinned function cannot call browser APIs directly
 Fix: remove the `#Target(Wasm)` pin, move browser work into a `#Target(JS)` function, or drop the browser API calls
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E-WEB-TARGET-BROWSER

Error [E-APP-TARGET-FEATURE]: App feature `.csr` needs target `JS`, but the resolved target is `Wasm`.
  --> tests/ui/app_capability_target.jet:4:27
    |
  4 | fn run() App -> web.app().csr()
    |                           ^^^
 Why: App is one type across targets, but each feature must be supported by the target selected by `#Target` or the package manifest; rejecting it in sema keeps AOT, JIT, interpreter, and web codegen on one meaning (I9).
 Fix: choose a build target that supports `.csr` (for example `#Target(JS)` for browser features or a native target for server features), or remove that feature.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E-APP-TARGET-FEATURE
